subject: Add data to ONE facet in ggplot

messages.author: 9cbdcb011f8600fa
messages.subject: Add data to ONE facet in ggplot
parts:
I am hoping this is my last ggplot question for awhile... almost there!

I am plotting two categories of grass cover with confidence intervals across 7 different treatments. 
For 6 treatments I have data across a 25 week period. For the first treatment I only have data for the very last week. 
I plotted confidence intervals around the data points/lines for the last 6 treatments that I have all data for, and would like to visualize some estimate of variance for the treatment that has only one data point per grass category (in the form of SE bars). 
I have successfully plotted either all SE bars across all treatments, or CIs for the last 6 treatments but no estimate of variance on the 1st treatment. 

I have tried multiple approaches over the last few days, to no avail. 
I tried doing it with two different data frames (that didn't work, it says I have an object of class uneval). 
I tried doing it with one data frame (the code you see below) and having it adding error bars only to the 1st treatment. Also didn't work (error is that object 'x' not found). 

I see a lot of people on the interweb who are wanting to do similar things (but not quite that), or those that want to do the same thing but who have received no response to their question (booooooo!). 

Here is a chunk of my code and what the graph currently looks like without error bars on the 1st treatment is attached as a .png: 

gplot(data=Merge2) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(x=Monitoring.Event, ymin=lower, ymax = upper, fill =Per.Ann), alpha=0.5) + 
  geom_line(aes(x=Monitoring.Event,y=mean, col=Per.Ann), size = 1.25) + 
  geom_point(aes(x=Monitoring.Event,y=mean, colour = Per.Ann), size = 4) + 
  facet_wrap(~Treatment, nrow=1) +
  geom_errorbar(data = subset(Merge2, Treatment == "Control Unburned"), aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se), width = 2, size = 1, inherit.aes=FALSE)

Thank you again in advance for applying your brilliant brains to my probably very simple problem with this same darn graph! 

Kristina

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Add data to ONE facet in ggplot
parts:
On Thu, Apr 23, 2015 at 10:38 AM, Kristina Wolf <kmw...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se)

Something like this:

library(ggplot2)


ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt)) +
geom_point() +
facet_grid(. ~ cyl)

mtcarsaddendum <- data.frame(mpg = 15, wt = 5, lab = "Text", cyl = factor(8,levels = c("4","6","8")), mean= 3, se= 1.5)

ggplot() +
geom_point(data=mtcars, aes(x= mpg, y=wt)) +
geom_errorbar(data = mtcarsaddendum, aes(x = mpg, y= wt, ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se)) +
facet_grid(. ~ cyl)

HTH, 
B

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Add data to ONE facet in ggplot
parts:
​

Took some fiddling but it worked! I cannot get it to recognize my factor levels to change the error bars to match the color of the points (I would like that), but if I can’t do that I will take this as is.
Thank you Brandon!

Here is the updated code and graph if anyone is interested

​ 
(I am sure there is a nicer, cleaner way to write it, but again, it’s me writing this, so be warned​ - there are probably extraneous pieces of code here, or more eloquent ways to write it​)​:​

KIN_addendum_annual <- data.frame(Monitoring.Event = 25, Per.Ann = "Annual grass",mean = 19, Treatment = factor("Control Unburned",levels = c("Control Unburned", "Control Burned", "1-2 Burned", "2-2 Burned", "4-2 Burned", "4-3 Burned", "4-4 Burned")), mean.1= 19, se= 2.685942240)
KIN_addendum_annual$Per.Ann = droplevels(KIN_addendum_annual$Per.Ann)
KIN_addendum_perennial <- data.frame(Monitoring.Event = 25, mean = 41, Per.Ann = "Perennial grass", Treatment = factor("Control Unburned",levels = c("Control Unburned", "Control Burned", "1-2 Burned", "2-2 Burned", "4-2 Burned", "4-3 Burned", "4-4 Burned")), mean= 41, se= 5.548487567)
KIN_addendum_perennial$Per.Ann = droplevels(KIN_addendum_perennial$Per.Ann)
KIN_addendum = rbind(KIN_addendum_annual, KIN_addendum_perennial)
KIN_addendum$Per.Ann = droplevels(KIN_addendum$Per.Ann)

ggplot(data=KIN.Aug.Per.Seed.sum) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(x=Monitoring.Event, ymin=lower, ymax = upper, fill =Per.Ann), alpha=0.5) + 
  geom_line(aes(x=Monitoring.Event,y=mean, col=Per.Ann), size = 1.25) + 
   facet_wrap(~Treatment, nrow=1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(x = Monitoring.Event, y = mean, ymin = mean.1 - se, ymax = mean.1 + se), data = KIN_addendum, width = 2, size = 1, inherit.aes=FALSE) + 
  geom_point(aes(x=Monitoring.Event,y=mean, colour = Per.Ann), size = 4) +  
  xlab("Monitoring Week (8/14/2013 - 5/5/2014)") + ylab("Mean Percent Cover (+- 2sd)") + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(seq(1,25,by=3))) + scale_y_continuous (limits = c(0,80), oob = rescale_none) +
  ggtitle("Mean Cover each monitoring week, August watering") + 
  scale_fill_discrete(name="Grass Type", breaks=c("Annual grass","Native grass"), labels=c("Annual grass cover","Perennial grass cover")) + 
  scale_colour_discrete(name="Grass Type", breaks=c("Annual grass","Native grass"), labels=c("Annual grass cover","Perennial grass cover")) + 
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank() ,
        strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size=20),
        strip.background = element_rect(colour="blue", fill="#CCCCFF"), 
        plot.title = element_text(face="bold", size=30), 
        axis.title.x = element_text(face="bold", size=20),
        axis.text.x  = element_text(face="bold", size=10),
        axis.title.y = element_text(face="bold", size=20),
        axis.text =element_text(face="bold", size=20),
        legend.text=element_text(face="bold", size=25),
        legend.title=element_text(size=30))

​
~ Kristina

One more addition, thanks to Noam. I wanted those error bars to be the same color as the points, but I was mapping the colors incorrectly because I had three factors (not two, like I intended) in one of the two dataframes from which I was pulling my datapoints. I also wanted to specify the colors myself, so I had to define the object with the colors I wanted.

Here is the corrected code and graphic:

KIN_addendum_annual <- data.frame(Monitoring.Event = 25, Per.Ann = "Annual grass",mean = 19, Treatment = factor("Control Unburned",levels = c("Control Unburned", "Control Burned", "1-2 Burned", "2-2 Burned", "4-2 Burned", "4-3 Burned", "4-4 Burned")), mean.1= 19, se= 2.685942240

)
KIN_addendum_annual$Per.Ann = droplevels(KIN_addendum_annual$Per.Ann)
KIN_addendum_perennial <- data.frame(Monitoring.Event = 25, mean = 41, Per.Ann = "Native grass", Treatment = factor("Control Unburned",levels = c("Control Unburned", "Control Burned", "1-2 Burned", "2-2 Burned", "4-2 Burned", "4-3 Burned", "4-4 Burned")), mean= 41, se= 5.548487567)
KIN_addendum_perennial$Per.Ann = droplevels(KIN_addendum_perennial$Per.Ann)
KIN_addendum = rbind(KIN_addendum_annual, KIN_addendum_perennial)
KIN_addendum$Per.Ann = droplevels(KIN_addendum$Per.Ann)

KIN.Aug.Per.Seed.sum = subset(KIN.Aug.Per.Seed.sum, KIN.Aug.Per.Seed.sum$Per.Ann !="")
KIN.Aug.Per.Seed.sum$Per.Ann = droplevels(KIN.Aug.Per.Seed.sum$Per.Ann)
levels(KIN.Aug.Per.Seed.sum$Per.Ann)
levels(KIN_addendum$Per.Ann)

col = c("#CC79A7", "#009E73")
ggplot(data=KIN.Aug.Per.Seed.sum) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(x=Monitoring.Event, ymin=lower, ymax = upper, fill =Per.Ann), alpha=0.5) + 
  geom_line(aes(x=Monitoring.Event,y=mean, col=Per.Ann), size = 1.25) + 
    facet_wrap(~Treatment, nrow=1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(x = Monitoring.Event, y = mean, ymin = mean.1 - se, ymax = mean.1 + se, colour = Per.Ann), data = KIN_addendum, width = 2, size = 1, inherit.aes=FALSE) + 
  geom_point(aes(x=Monitoring.Event,y=mean, colour = Per.Ann), size = 4) +  
  xlab("Monitoring Week (8/14/2013 - 5/5/2014)") + ylab("Mean Percent Cover (+- 2sd)") + 
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(seq(1,25,by=3))) + scale_y_continuous (limits = c(0,80), oob = rescale_none) +
  ggtitle("Mean Cover each monitoring week, August watering") + 
  scale_fill_manual(name="Grass Type", breaks=c("Annual grass","Native grass"), labels=c("Annual grass cover","Perennial grass cover"), values = col) + 
  scale_colour_manual(name="Grass Type", breaks=c("Annual grass","Native grass"), labels=c("Annual grass cover","Perennial grass cover"), values = col) + 
  guides(fill=guide_legend(reverse=TRUE), 
         colour=guide_legend(reverse=TRUE)) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank() ,
        strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size=20),
        strip.background = element_rect(colour="blue", fill="#CCCCFF"), 
        plot.title = element_text(face="bold", size=30), 
        axis.title.x = element_text(face="bold", size=20),
        axis.text.x  = element_text(face="bold", size=10),
        axis.title.y = element_text(face="bold", size=20),
        axis.text =element_text(face="bold", size=20),
        legend.text=element_text(face="bold", size=25),
        legend.title=element_text(size=30))

​
